clue.text: Talk as if mad at university party

blocks.note: to rave is to talk wildly, as if out of one's mind
a British student who is in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone babbling like a lunatic at a student party.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to university and come down when you leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave-up is informal British slang for a lively, noisy celebration.

clue.text: Devotee turned up, on time, in disgust

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a devotee is a lover of something
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fan arriving punctually but in a state of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the time after the reversed devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to revolt someone is to sicken or repel them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See one in travel documents opposite number

indicators.note: the first pair of items sits inside the second, which wraps around them

blocks.note: V abbreviates Latin vide, meaning see, as in cross-references
the Roman numeral for one
visas are entry permits stamped in passports

explanation.surface: A tip to check a single item among one's passport papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A vis-a-vis is a counterpart, someone holding the equivalent position elsewhere.

clue.text: Complete lunatic blowing top

indicators.note: losing its top means the word for the madman sheds its first letter in this down light

blocks.note: British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total madman losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective for the lunatic but is the definition; 'blowing top' doubles as losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and complete are both intensifying adjectives meaning absolute or total.

clue.text: Field sport record taken by American

blocks.note: a gramophone record is a disc
US is the abbreviation for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: An American athlete setting a record in a track-and-field event.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus throw is one of the field events in athletics, as opposed to track races.

clue.text: One right in front of habitual customer is somewhat odd

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
R is the usual abbreviation for right
a regular is someone who frequents a pub or shop

explanation.surface: A person standing in front of a pub regular strikes one as rather strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular describes something out of the ordinary or not conforming to the norm, hence a little odd.

clue.text: Representative has turn under company car

indicators.note: in a down light, being under something means sitting below it, so that word is written second

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
a Member of Parliament represents a constituency
a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A sales rep gets a go in the firm's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'under' puts the first pieces below the company, so CO comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a small family car, a common class of vehicle.

clue.text: Evildoer, reportedly one who sided with Brutus

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the name sounds

blocks.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators who joined Brutus against Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: Calling one of Caesar's assassins a wrongdoer, as Shakespeare's audience might.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar a second Cinna, the poet, is killed by the mob for sharing the conspirator's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner is someone who commits wrongs, so an evildoer in moral terms.

clue.text: Distinguished guest, female one, excited Virginians met outside

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lady guest greeted on the doorstep by a crowd of thrilled Americans from Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of female, one, Virginians and met are rearranged; 'outside' only adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A visiting fireman is an American idiom for a VIP visitor given lavish hospitality.

clue.text: Easy? Not tonight, I suspect

indicators.note: a suspect account is dubious, hinting that the preceding letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doubtful reply to a casual suggestion: not this evening, I think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' serves twice in the surface but only once as fodder; 'suspect' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a task is simple, requiring hardly any effort.

clue.text: Locust in a Calais café? Unlikely

indicators.note: an unlikely version is an improbable one, so the letters are set in an improbable order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doubting that a swarming insect would turn up in a French port's coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locust' looks like the insect, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The false acacia, Robinia pseudoacacia, is also known as the black locust tree.

clue.text: Young creature that's always allowed to go round

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: let means permitted
ever can mean always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A little animal that is permitted to wander about at will.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, a young animal.

clue.text: Toboggan carrying crack in suitcases

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying a load holds it inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a luge is a small racing sledge
a crack is a joke, as is a gag

explanation.surface: A sledge transporting a fractured load in its cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' suggests a split, but here it is a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the collective term for bags and suitcases taken on a journey.

clue.text: Go over on plane to find rented property?

blocks.note: to service a machine is to go over it, checking and repairing
a plane is a flat level surface

explanation.surface: Checking over an aircraft to locate a leased home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' points to aircraft but means a level surface; a service flat is a British term for a rented apartment with cleaning included.
explanation.definitionFit: A service flat is an apartment let together with domestic services such as cleaning, so a rental.

clue.text: Argument about a native in centre of Bangkok

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the one with equal letters on either side

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a native of a place is its son, as in a native son
taken as written
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A dispute concerning a local person in downtown Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a placement word but is simply kept as the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument can be a line of reasoning, a chain of logic offered in support.

clue.text: Eccentric gets in loads — with these?

definitions.text: Eccentric gets in loads — with these?

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the first word goes inside the second

blocks.note: a charge is a load, as in a charge of powder in a gun
a card is an amusingly odd person

explanation.surface: An oddball buys up masses of goods, perhaps on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: an odd character gets in loads of shopping with the help of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge cards let shoppers buy plenty now and settle the bill later.

clue.text: Cold, supple mountaineer?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
limber means flexible, supple

explanation.surface: A chilly but agile alpinist.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition stretches: a climbing plant scales walls as a mountaineer scales peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber is anyone who climbs mountains, or by extension a plant that grows upward.

clue.text: Drink wine in base

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in sips
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Having a glass of wine back at camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement word but only joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A base or foundation is what holds something up, a support.

clue.text: Dog twice fetches fluffy ball

blocks.note: a Pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog
the dog is repeated

explanation.surface: A dog retrieving a soft ball for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small decorative tuft of wool, like the fluffy ball on a bobble hat.

clue.text: Later, served up a dumpling

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up means writing it from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: not now is a way of saying later

explanation.surface: A dish brought out afterwards to the diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' fits the food picture but also flips the phrase in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonton is a Chinese dumpling of filled dough, often in soup.

clue.text: Gold coin, foreign, found next to ring in river

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the word is made strange by mixing its letters

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A gold foreign coin and a ring turn up in a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major river in South America, flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Plays, relaxing in company, a West Indian ballad

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters are freed to settle in a new order
one word placed in another sits inside it, wrapped on both sides

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone playing a laid-back Caribbean song among friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a Caribbean song style from Trinidad, often topical, a kind of ballad.

clue.text: Girl's love for Belgian composer

blocks.note: lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A young woman's affection for a Flemish musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando di Lasso, born in Mons, was a Renaissance composer of the Franco-Flemish school.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasso, also called Lassus, came from Mons in what is now Belgium, so a Belgian composer.

clue.text: Open, entrance for buses etc

blocks.note: open to all is public
to entrance is to delight, and transport means rapture

explanation.surface: A doorway left open for vehicles to pass through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to enchant, matched by the noun transport, as in transports of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses, trams and trains run for general use make up public transport.

clue.text: Silver in bog? That's an illusion

indicators.note: the precious metal is placed in the marsh, which surrounds it

blocks.note: a mire is a bog or swamp
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Seeing silver glinting in a swamp turns out to be imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen shimmering in a desert.

clue.text: See good thing across street in US city

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An invitation to view a fine sight across the road in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is split: a see in a US city, since the Catholic Archdiocese of Boston is a see.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat; Boston, Massachusetts, is the seat of an archdiocese as well as a city.
